advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make _snapshot_in_head distinguish a genuine 'absent from HEAD' (git rc 1/128 for a missing path) from a transient/tooling git failure, and fail SAFE (do NOT revert) on ambiguous non-zero results.
evidence: '_git' is run_git_write(..., check=False), which returns transient faults verbatim: run_git_write folds a watchdog timeout into 'a synthetic rc-124 result' and index-lock exhaustion into a non-zero return (src/rebar/_store/gitutil.py:526,554)
The revert branch is gated on 'not _snapshot_in_head(...)' (compact_recovery.py:157), and _revert_partial_fold both renames .retired back and removes the snapshot (compact_recovery.py:118-130)

Test confirms committed folds retain on-disk .retired files: tests/unit/test_compact_crash_atomicity.py 'assert retired_before, "precondition: the fold retired its sources"' — so a false negative reverts a committed fold rather than being a harmless no-op
advisory.finding: compact_recovery._snapshot_in_head treats every non-zero git returncode as 'snapshot absent from HEAD', but run_git_write(check=False) also returns non-zero on transient faults (index.lock exhaustion, rc-124 timeout, transient runner-FS faults). Because a committed fold keeps its *.retired source files on disk, a transient false-negative here drives _revert_partial_fold to rename retired sources back to active and os.remove() the already-committed SNAPSHOT — corrupting a landed fold and dirtying the shared tree, the very wedge this feature prevents.
scenarios: A transient git index.lock/object-store fault or watchdog timeout during the recovery preamble while a legitimately-committed fold journal is still pending (crash between commit and journal discard)
advisory.suggested_fix: Only treat the snapshot as absent when git reports the specific not-found condition; on any other non-zero (timeout rc-124, lock exhaustion, cat-file fatal errors unrelated to a missing path) skip the revert and leave the journal for a later pass, so recovery never destroys a committed fold on a transient fault.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test where a live journal's recorded snapshot is absent from disk and assert recover_abandoned_folds discards the journal and reverts nothing.
evidence: Module docstring bullet: 'a journal whose snapshot is gone from disk ⇒ ... discard the journal, touch nothing'
search of tests/unit for write_intent shows only the committed-snapshot (line 219) and round-trip (line 319) cases — no missing-snapshot case
advisory.finding: The 'journal whose snapshot is gone from disk' recovery branch (superseded/fsck-repaired state) is documented as a distinct discrimination outcome but has no test: recover_abandoned_folds only reverts when os.path.exists(snapshot_path) AND not in HEAD, and no test drives a live journal whose snapshot is absent from disk to assert it discards the journal and touches nothing.
scenarios: A journalled fold whose snapshot was removed by fsck --repair-snapshots or superseded; a regression that made recovery attempt a revert (or crash) on a missing snapshot
advisory.suggested_fix: Write an intent whose snapshot path does not exist on disk, run recover_abandoned_folds_locked, assert it returns 0, leaves the tree unchanged, and discards the journal.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that monkeypatches compact_recovery.write_intent to raise OSError and asserts the fold returns 1 and leaves the tree unmutated (no SNAPSHOT, no retired sources, clean porcelain).
evidence: compact_txn.py:414-422 `except OSError: ... sys.stderr.write('Error: cannot journal the compaction fold ...') return 1`
search of tests for 'refusing to mutate' returns (no matches)
advisory.finding: The write_intent-fails refusal path is untested: when the intent journal cannot be written, _apply_fold logs, emits an Error to stderr, and returns 1 without mutating the store — an observable error contract with no coverage.
scenarios: Journal directory unwritable / OSError from write_intent — the fold must refuse rather than mutate the worktree without its crash sentinel
advisory.suggested_fix: monkeypatch compact_recovery.write_intent to raise OSError, run _fold, assert rc==1, no snapshots, no retired, _status(repo)=='' .

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that forces a reverse-rename failure during _rollback_fold and asserts the SNAPSHOT is retained (not removed) and the journal is discarded.
evidence: compact_txn.py:356-378 `rollback_clean = True ... except OSError: rollback_clean = False ... if rollback_clean: os.remove(final_path) else: (retained)`
search of tests/unit for 'rollback_clean' returns (no matches)
test_recovery_never_touches_snapshot_inconsistent_without_journal reconstructs the mixed state manually (lines 236-238) rather than exercising the guard
advisory.finding: The incomplete-rollback data-loss guard is untested: when a reverse-rename fails (rollback_clean=False), _rollback_fold must RETAIN the uncommitted SNAPSHOT (rather than delete it and drop the folded events) as the SNAPSHOT_INCONSISTENT state. The existing fsck test only reconstructs that state by hand and never drives _rollback_fold into the failed-rename branch.
scenarios: A reverse-rename fails during rollback (e.g. os.rename raises); the SNAPSHOT must be kept so the folded event is not silently dropped
advisory.suggested_fix: Trigger _abort_fold with an injected os.rename OSError on one fold source and assert the SNAPSHOT file still exists afterward while the intent journal is discarded.

blocking.finding: bugfix-size-attestation: this change touches 392 non-test line(s) — over the 150-line floor for a bug fix — but bug e72e-259d-5ee7-4e73 has no acceptable plan-review attestation (verdict: unsigned; no plan-review attestation record). A fix this large is a design change wearing a bug label: write the fix plan into the ticket's description, run `rebar review-plan e72e-259d-5ee7-4e73` (it auto-escalates a bug with non-test file impact to the full review and SIGNS an attestation on a PASS; if the review passed but no attestation landed, `rebar sign-review e72e-259d-5ee7-4e73` re-persists it cheaply, and `rebar review-plan e72e-259d-5ee7-4e73 --status` confirms it is current without an LLM call), then re-push.
